title: Food Safety and Cooking During Power Cuts
summary: Managing refrigerated and frozen food safely during outages and preventing carbon monoxide poisoning.
content:
1. Keep Fridge and Freezer Closed:
- Avoid opening doors unnecessarily to preserve internal temperatures.
- An unopened fridge keeps food safely cold for roughly 4 hours.
- An unopened full freezer will keep food frozen for approximately 48 hours (24 hours if half-full).

2. Discarding Spoiled Food:
- Discard perishable food (raw or cooked meat, fish, dairy, eggs, cooked pasta/rice, and leftovers) that has been warmer than 8°C for more than 2 hours.
- Never taste food to determine if it is safe. Discard items showing foul smell, slime, or discoloration.

3. UK Food Standards Agency (FSA) Refreezing Guidance:
- Food that has partially thawed but still retains ice crystals throughout may be safely refrozen or cooked immediately.
- Food that has completely defrosted but remained below 4°C can be thoroughly cooked to steaming hot throughout, after which it can be safely refrozen as a prepared meal.
- If thawed food has reached room temperature, dispose of it safely.

4. Critical Carbon Monoxide (CO) Safety:
- NEVER use outdoor camping stoves, gas canister burners, charcoal barbecues, or paraffin heaters indoors or inside an enclosed porch.
- Carbon monoxide is an invisible, odourless, and deadly gas that builds rapidly in enclosed spaces.
- Use only designated indoor gas appliances that have functioning flue systems, or consume ready-to-eat, non-cook emergency food rations.
